samples.summary: Share-link PDF path mounts CollabDocumentProvider outside the new NonDurableScope guard
samples.evidence: `SharedDocumentInner` early-returns `<SharedPdfLayout .../>` at shared-document.tsx:968 (see the `SharedPdfLayout` definition at :742 and its own `<YorkieProvider>` at :753) — i.e. *before* the `<NonDurableScope>` wrapper the diff adds at :1016. `SharedPdfLayout` renders `PdfCollabProvider`, which renders `CollabDocumentProvider` (packages/frontend/src/app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:200). So one of the two share-link Yorkie subtrees never passes through the guard the diff introduces, and the test added in `src/app/shared/__tests__/shared-document-durability.test.tsx` only exercises the non-PDF branch (its `resolveShareLink` mock returns `type: 'sheet'`). Today nothing leaks, because `useDurableDocument` separately refuses `pdf-` keys (packages/frontend/src/lib/use-durable-document.ts:41) — the guard is covered only by that second, unrelated exclusion. The fix belongs on `shared-document.tsx`: hoist `NonDurableScope` above the type dispatch so every share-link branch is inside it.

samples.summary: New ['me','optional'] observer in CollabDocumentProvider has staleTime 0, defeating sheet-view's 5-minute cache window and adding a GET /auth/me per editor mount
samples.evidence: `sheet-view.tsx:212-216` observes `queryKey: ["me", "optional"]` with `staleTime: 5 * 60 * 1000` precisely so re-mounts do not re-request. `collab-document-provider.tsx:181-188` now adds a second observer on the *same* key with no `staleTime` (App.tsx:89 constructs `new QueryClient()` with defaults, so staleTime is 0) and an `initialData` factory. Because `CollabDocumentProvider` is the ancestor of `SheetView` on `/s/:id`, its observer mounts first and forces a refetch of `['me','optional']` on every document open — an extra `GET /auth/me` per editor mount for all users, including on builds where the offline feature is entirely off (`@yorkie-js/react` is pinned 0.7.22 in packages/frontend/package.json:66, below `MinClientKeyVersion` 0.7.23). Same key is also observed by `PublicRoute.tsx:12` and `shared-document.tsx:936`. Setting a `staleTime` on the provider's query, or gating it behind `mayPersist`, would keep the existing consumers' behaviour.

samples.summary: OfflineRuntime runs its full housekeeping — including an unconditional GET /documents and creating the IndexedDB database — on every authenticated session even though this build cannot persist anything
samples.evidence: `PrivateRoute.tsx:30` now mounts `<OfflineRuntime>` for every signed-in session. Its effect unconditionally constructs a `WafflebaseDocStore` (opening/creating `wafflebase-offline`), runs `retryPendingOfflineErase`, `store.collectStale()`, and `await fetchDocuments()` followed by `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments`. None of this is gated on `supportsClientKey()` or on the offline preference, and with `@yorkie-js/react` pinned to 0.7.22 (packages/frontend/package.json:66) `supportsClientKey()` is false, so no document can ever have been stored. The observable blast radius on the existing app is a new `GET /documents` request per session (via `fetchWithAuth`, whose 401 arm triggers logout+redirect) and a new IndexedDB database created for every user. Gating the effect on `supportsClientKey()` would make the feature's rollout genuinely inert.

samples.summary: Every 401 anywhere in the app now blocks on an IndexedDB erase before redirecting to /login
samples.evidence: `logout()` now awaits `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` (api/auth.ts, added before the redirect). `logout()` is called from `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm at api/auth.ts:251, which is the shared failure path for every API module in the frontend (`api/miro.ts:1`, `api/lakehouse.ts:1`, `api/images.ts:1`, `api/documents.ts:3`, `api/workspaces.ts` …), and from `components/nav-user.tsx:41`. `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` opens a `WafflebaseDocStore` whenever `offlineUserId()` is set — which `OfflineRuntime` sets for every signed-in session via `rememberOfflineUser` — so the session-expiry redirect now waits on an IndexedDB open + `dropAllForUser` sweep even on builds where nothing was ever persisted.

samples.summary: deleteDocument's new offline purge now runs on the create-rollback paths that use it as cleanup
samples.evidence: `api/documents.ts:167` adds `await purgeOfflineDocuments([id])` to the success branch of `deleteDocument`. Two callers use `deleteDocument` purely as rollback for a document they just created and that was never opened: `packages/frontend/src/app/documents/upload-queue.ts:237` (`deleteDoc: deleteDocument`) and `packages/frontend/src/app/documents/miro-import-runner.ts:79`. Each rollback now additionally opens and closes the `wafflebase-offline` IndexedDB (whenever an offline user id is recorded) before the rollback completes — a new per-failure cost on an error path that was previously a single DELETE. Harmless functionally, but neither call site was considered and a bulk-upload failure will do this once per queued file.

samples.summary: handleOf's new `id` fallback and mapDescendants can overwrite a mapper `__id` → realId entry on the Miro import path
samples.evidence: `handleOf` (apply-imported-content.ts:63-65) now falls back to `element.id`, and `mapDescendants` (:75-84) writes `realIds.set(handle, child.id)` for every nested child of every group — including on the existing Miro import path, which previously only ever populated the map from `__id`. `realIds` is a single flat `Map`, so a group child whose `id` happens to equal a top-level element's `__id` (Miro item ids and mapper handles are drawn from different namespaces, but nothing enforces disjointness) now silently replaces that element's `__id → realId` entry, and `remapEndpoint` would point a connector at the child instead. The board import path is the out-of-diff consumer: `applyImportedContent`'s `board` branch at apply-imported-content.ts:281 feeds `mapMiroItems` output straight through. Confirming would need `mapMiroItems`' element shape (does it emit both `__id` and `id`?) — I could not determine that from the diff.

finding.summary: Any single 401 anywhere in the app now erases every live offline entry — including non-empty unpushed change logs of documents currently open — from a call site unrelated to the user's intent
finding.evidence: `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:250-267) calls `logout({ eraseLocalData: 'keep-archives' })`, which reaches `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` → `WafflebaseDocStore.dropAllForUser`. `dropAllForUser` (packages/frontend/src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts, `dropAllForUser`) deliberately does NOT spare a document that is open (its own comment says so) and does not spare an entry whose change log is non-empty. Every other deletion path in this same store treats exactly those two conditions as inviolable: `evictOldest` skips any entry with `changeCount > 0` ("a non-empty log is work that may never have reached the server") and `collectStale` skips anything `isLive`. `fetchWithAuth` wraps essentially every request in the app — a notification poll, a sidebar `fetchWorkspaces`, the new `OfflineRuntime` `fetchDocuments()` — so a transient expired cookie or a backend restart, while an editor sits open with unpushed offline work, deletes the durable copy of that work. The inline comment at auth.ts:262-265 justifies it as "copies of content the server holds", which is true of the snapshot but not of the appended change log, which is by construction the un-pushed delta. Fix belongs on the erase call: the 401 path should spare entries with a non-empty log / open documents the way eviction and collection do.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. auth.ts:250-267 calls logout({eraseLocalData:"keep-archives"}); logout (auth.ts:125-127) awaits eraseOfflineDataOnLogout, which reaches WafflebaseDocStore.dropAllForUser (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1031-1075). That method loops every header key for the user and calls purge (827-835), which deletes snapshot, header and the entire change range with no archive — unlike remove (757-816). dropAllForUser's own comment (1037-1041) confirms it does not spare an open document, and it never consults changeCount. This contradicts the invariant the store's other deletion paths enforce: evictOldest skips entries with changeCount > 0 (1362, rationale 1332-1341: "a non-empty log is work that may never have reached the server") and collectStale skips isLive entries (1115-1121); purgeDocument offers skipOpen/updatedSince (869-901). keepArchives only spares pre-existing archives (1071-1073) and does nothing for a live entry's un-pushed log. The path is broadly reachable: fetchWithAuth has 85 call sites across 19 frontend files (notifications polling, workspaces, documents), so a transient expired cookie or backend restart triggers a whole-device erase of live entries from a call site unrelated to user intent. No guard elsewhere archives or spares non-empty logs before this erase. Impact is loss of the durable copy of un-pushed work — data loss on a reachable path (critical); the remaining doubt is only frequency, which does not reduce impact.
